The 'lazy beats perfect' finding is UNRELIABLE. (2) HIGH: Loss aversion switches 1 month late + uses sum not compound. (3) MEDIUM: Panic goes to GLD not cash as described. (4) MEDIUM: t-test invalid (needs HAC/DM). FOMO finding (-58% Sharpe) LIKELY SAFE: simple override logic, no timing bug identified. 'FOMO > Panic in cost' is the key publishable takeaway.

title: K744: 5-Min RV Data Validation — AC(1)=0.423 confirms daily proxy ceiling, U-shape moderate
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K744: DATA VALIDATION of 51 days SPY 5-min data (2026-01-14 to 2026-03-27). Part A: Data quality good — mean 76 bars/day, only 3/51 flagged (2 partial days + 1 gap). Part B: CRITICAL FINDING — RV AC(1)=0.423 vs daily r² AC(1)=0.076, confirming K196 (0.414 vs -0.118). Daily proxies are poor: |r| Spearman ρ=0.196, r² Spearman ρ=0.196, GARCH σ² Spearman ρ=0.107 — all insignificant (p>0.2). Mean r²/RV ratio=1.83 (overestimates) but median=0.80 (high variance). Part C: U-shape present but moderate (ratio=1.258). First 30 min = 19.6% of daily RV, last 30 min = 6.5%, combined 26%. First-vs-middle t=13.1 (p<0.001), last-vs-middle not significant (p=0.066). HAR-RV pilot feasible with 51 days but estimation window tight. KEY INSIGHT: The 5.6x AC(1) gap (0.423 vs 0.076) is the fundamental reason GARCH has a ceiling on daily data — RV is much more predictable than daily squared returns.
evidence: AC(1) RV_5min = 0.423 vs AC(1) r² = 0.076 (5.6x gap)
Proxy correlations: |r| ρ=0.196, r² ρ=0.196, GARCH σ² ρ=0.107 — all insignificant
U-shape ratio 1.258, first 30 min = 19.6% of daily RV

title: K745: Pilot HAR-RV with 5-Min Data — HAR-ABS daily proxy beats HAR-RV (N=37, preliminary)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K745: PILOT HAR-RV with 51 days SPY 5-min data (2026-01-14 to 2026-03-27, N_OOS=37). PRELIMINARY — below 252-day OOS minimum. Part A: Realized measures computed — mean RV annualized vol 11.1%, jump fraction low (4.8%), AC(1)=0.423, ADF stationary (t=-4.41). Part B: In-sample HAR-RV R²=0.16 (N=41), β_daily=0.385 (t=2.35, only significant coef). Part C: 11 models compared. SURPRISE RESULT: HAR-ABS (daily |r| proxy targeting RV) ranks #1 (QLIKE=0.077, R²=0.41, MZ-R²=0.41), beating HAR-RV (QLIKE=0.109, R²=0.35, MZ-R²=0.39). HAR framework dominates: top 4 are all HAR variants. GJR-GARCH (QLIKE=0.157) and EWMA (0.207) much worse. VIX-implied and Naive-RV worst. Part D: No DM significant except VIX-implied (DM=-6.47). Why daily proxy wins with N=37: (1) HAR-ABS has 51 training points all sharing the same target (RV), while HAR-RV features need 5-22 day rolling → fewer usable rows; (2) Corr(RV_5min, r²_daily) same-day only 0.119 — daily r² is a very noisy proxy, but HAR-ABS learns the mapping from |r| patterns to RV over sufficient training; (3) With longer samples HAR-RV should overtake (literature R²=0.3-0.6 at N=500+). Key: methodology validated — pipeline works end-to-end. Next: 60 days (~April 11) for more stable estimation.

title: K746: ★★ Bitcoin Volatility and VIX — Crypto Fear Channel is Asymmetric
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Bitcoin-VIX relationship is ASYMMETRIC: BTC vol Granger-causes VIX changes (F=8.5, p=0.004 at lag-1) but VIX does NOT predict BTC vol (F=2.9, p=0.086). The 'fear channel' runs FROM crypto TO TradFi, not reverse. Full-sample VIX-BTC_RV correlation is weak (r=0.178) vs VIX-SPY_RV (r=0.805). STRUCTURAL BREAK confirmed (Fisher z=-6.63, p<0.001): BTC-SPY daily correlation jumped from 0.138 (pre-2021) to 0.371 (2021+), consistent with institutional adoption increasing coupling. BTC vol (66.7% ann) is 3.8x SPY (17.7%). When SPY crashes >2%, BTC also negative 71% of times (mean -3.0%). VIX regime matters: BTC mean return is +42 bps/day in low VIX (<15) but -72 bps/day in extreme VIX (>35), with BTC-SPY correlation rising from 0.067 to 0.569 across regimes. COVID crash was COUPLED (BTC -33%, SPY -34%, corr 0.61); crypto winter 2022 was DECOUPLED from equity markets. Portfolio: 5% BTC in 50/50 SPY/GLD improves Sharpe from 1.060 to 1.278 (2015-2026), but MDD worsens from -20.3% to -20.8%. VIX-conditioned BTC allocation (remove BTC when VIX>25, lag=1) reduces Sharpe slightly vs static (1.247 vs 1.278 for 5% BTC) due to TX costs (20bps). Best static allocation: 20% BTC with Sharpe 1.449 but MDD -30.7%. Key insight: BTC is NOT a safe haven — it amplifies TradFi stress. The asymmetric Granger causality (crypto→TradFi but not reverse) is novel and could be a paper contribution.

title: Codex Review K746: 2 HIGH (Granger tests backward RV + structural break wrong variable), descriptive safe
content: [提出: Codex, 執行: Claude] K746 review: (1) HIGH: Granger tests whether lagged VIX explains changes in backward-looking 22d BTC RV — NOT whether VIX predicts future BTC vol. 'Asymmetric fear channel' claim methodology needs fix. (2) HIGH: Fisher z-test uses BTC-SPY daily return corr, not VIX-BTC RV corr as claimed. Hard-coded 2021 split, not real break detection. (3) MEDIUM: Regime classification ex-post. (4) LOW: shift(1) correct, TX consistent. DESCRIPTIVE findings (BTC not safe haven, tail dependence, coupling increase) likely directionally correct. Granger claim needs proper forward-looking RV target to be publishable.

title: K747: Equal Risk Contribution (ERC) Portfolio — Risk Budgeting Without Timing
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] ERC (Maillard et al 2010) equalizes marginal risk contributions via optimization. Tested 2/3/4-asset ERC vs static 50/50 SPY/GLD with proper monthly hold-and-drift rebalancing (fixing K737 Codex bug). RESULTS: 2-asset ERC Sharpe=1.795 vs 50/50 Sharpe=1.849 (diff=-0.054, DM t=-1.019 NS). ERC ≈ InvVol for 2-asset (both 1.795) — confirms K704: when SPY vol(19.0%)≈GLD vol(18.1%), all RP methods converge. Multi-asset ERC worse: 3-asset 1.492, 4-asset 1.396 (TLT drags). ERC+12/VIX=1.755, worse than static ERC. Cross-OOS: ERC 3/5 wins (wins in 2006-2018 periods, loses 2018-2026). Weight stability: SPY mean=0.504 std=0.085, annual turnover 1.66. TX cost impact negligible (0-50bps: 1.796→1.783). ERC vs InvVol diff: -0.21%/yr, practically zero. VERDICT: ERC is mathematically elegant but adds zero practical value over 50/50 SPY/GLD. The sophistication premium is effectively nil. Data: yfinance SPY/GLD/TLT/EEM 2005-2026.

title: The Simplicity Premium — Hypothesis REJECTED: Complex VIX-based strategies beat simple ones
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K748 tested whether simple strategies outperform complex ones (K740/K747/K737 suggested this). RESULT: Hypothesis REJECTED. 14 forward-tracked strategies (2023-01-04 to 2026-03-27). (A) Parameter count vs Sharpe: rho=+0.077 p=0.79 — NO correlation. Complex category avg Sharpe 2.51 > simple 2.03. (B) Turnover: rho=+0.749 p=0.002 — higher turnover = HIGHER Sharpe (not lower). TX cost explains only 9.7% of gap. (C) Regime robustness: rho=-0.066 p=0.82 — no complexity-regime link. Most regime-robust are momentum strategies (range 1.6), least robust are single-asset VT (range 10.4). (D) Bootstrap: simple underperforms complex by 0.47 Sharpe, 95% CI [-0.62, +0.05], P(simple worse)=0.95. (E) Composite rank: piecewise(moderate)>#1, adaptive_tier(complex)>#2, taiwan_spy_momentum(simple)>#3. KEY INSIGHT: DeMiguel (2009) 1/N result does NOT apply to VIX-based rule strategies because parameters are thresholds on OBSERVABLES (VIX), not estimates of future returns. No estimation error → no overfitting penalty → complexity can help. The real driver of performance is not simplicity but DESIGN QUALITY: the best strategy (piecewise_conservative) uses just 2 well-chosen parameters (VIX 12/20 breakpoints) to achieve Sharpe 3.16, MDD -2.5%.

title: K749: Yield Curve Slope and Equity Volatility — NULL for short-term, interesting long-horizon signal
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Yield curve slope (10Y-3M) tested as predictor of equity volatility. Data: ^TNX, ^IRX, SPY, ^VIX from yfinance, 2005-2026 (5337 obs). PART A: Slope mean=1.26%, std=1.23%, inverted 15.1% of days. 14 inversion episodes identified (major: 2006-2007 pre-GFC 272d, 2022-2024 post-rate-hikes 732d). Extremely persistent (AC lag1=0.999). Counter-intuitive: steep curve has HIGHEST VIX (22.6) — steep=crisis recovery. PART B: Univariate slope predicts fwd RV (t=2.5-2.9) but ALL information is subsumed by VIX. Partial corr controlling VIX: 21d=-0.006(NS), 63d=0.048(t=3.51), 126d=0.072(t=5.21), 252d=-0.005(NS). Tiny partial r at 63d/126d — statistically significant but economically negligible (<0.08). Granger causality all NS. PART C: Inversion event study — 252d forward vol ratio 1.37x (t=3.11, sig); 88% of inversions preceded VIX>30 within 1yr (vs 64% unconditional). But 21d/63d/126d all NS. Inversion is a long-lead warning, not short-term signal. PART D: No slope strategy beats 12/VIX (Sharpe 0.798). Best slope: combo 0.746 — actually significantly WORSE (DM=-2.87, p=0.004). PART E: Subsample instability — partial corr flips sign (2016-2020: -0.342 vs 2021-2026: +0.198). VERDICT: NULL for trading. Yield curve is too slow (months) for monthly VT. VIX already captures the relevant vol information. The only interesting finding: inversion predicts 12-month high-vol episodes (88% hit rate) but this is well-known from recession literature (Estrella & Hardouvelis 1991).

title: K750: Google Trends Fear Proxy — Real Alternative Data, NULL for Vol Prediction (VIX Sufficiency #36)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K750: Google Trends as Fear Proxy — tested REAL Google Trends search volume (pytrends) for 5 fear-related terms: "stock market crash", "recession", "VIX", "market crash", "bear market" (US, 2010-2026 weekly). Composite Google Fear Index (rolling z-score of 5 terms). N=797 weekly. Part A: Fear-VIX corr=0.421, Fear-RV corr=0.570, Fear-SPY ret corr=-0.286. Part B: In-sample ΔR²=0.0377 (VIX R²=0.486 → VIX+Fear 0.524), partial r|VIX=0.271 (t=7.92, sig). BUT OOS DM t=0.669 (Harvey FAIL, 744 forecasts). Part C: Fear Binary strategy Sharpe=0.834 < BH 50/50 0.938 < 12/VIX 0.904. DM vs BH t=-0.96 (NS). Part D: CRITICAL FINDING — peak cross-correlation at lag=0 (contemporaneous), NOT leading. Fear LAGS VIX at lag=-1 (r=0.306) > lag=+1 (r=0.369). Google searches are REACTIVE to market events, not predictive. Granger test: Fear(t-1) → ΔlnVIX(t) coef=-0.0216 (t=-2.71, sig) — but NEGATIVE sign means high fear predicts VIX DECREASE (mean-reversion, not escalation). Part E: Cross-OOS 1/5 FAIL. Conclusion: Google Trends search volume is genuine alternative data but does not beat VIX for either prediction or trading. In-sample partial correlation exists (0.271) but does not survive OOS. VIX sufficiency #36. References: Da, Engelberg & Gao (2015) RFS; Vlastakis & Markellos (2012) JBFA; Preis, Moat & Stanley (2013) Sci Rep.

title: K751: Overnight VIX News Sentiment Proxy — Statistically Significant but Economically Marginal
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K751: Overnight VIX change (close→open) as proxy for financial news sentiment. 4082 days (2010-2026). Part A: |overnight VIX Δ| correlates r=0.30 with next-day |SPY ret| (p<1e-86), but incremental R² over VIX level is only 0.45% (F=25.67, p<1e-6). Signed change much weaker r=0.075. Part B: Event-day detection strong—2σ overnight VIX moves predict 2.34x next-day vol (t=15.61). U-shaped quintile pattern: both extreme up and down overnight VIX changes predict higher vol. Direction does NOT matter (up vs down: p=0.52). Part C: Trading strategy HURTS: overnight-adjusted 12/VIX Sharpe 0.679 vs standard 0.788 (DM t=-2.68, p=0.0075). Extra turnover 12.37 annualized destroys any marginal signal. Part D: Higher thresholds (less adjustment) → closer to standard 12/VIX → better Sharpe. Part E: Rolling correlation varies 0-0.70, mean 0.22, 94% positive but unstable year-to-year. Part F: Signal stronger in high VIX regime (r=0.21) vs low VIX (r=0.08). Conclusion: overnight VIX carries real but tiny incremental info. As EVENT DETECTOR (rare extreme days) it works; as DAILY TRADING SIGNAL it fails after TX costs. Real NLP pipeline would need to beat this 0.45% R² ceiling significantly to be tradeable.

title: K752: ★★★ VIX Sufficiency Era Stability — TIME-INVARIANT across 33 years (1993-2026)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K752: VIX sufficiency era stability test across 5 eras spanning 33 years (1993-2026, 8325 obs). PART B — VIX prediction power: R² ranges 0.24 (low-vol QE era) to 0.64 (post-dot-com), mean 0.45, CV=0.33 — TIME-INVARIANT (CV<0.50). Lowest R²=0.24 in 2012-2020 low-vol era (VIX stuck near 15, less variation). Highest R²=0.64 in 2000-2007 (higher VIX range). Full sample R²=0.51, corr=0.72. All eras highly significant (all t>24). PART C — 12/VIX strategy: wins only 1/5 eras vs 50/50 baseline (only in low-vol QE era where VIX<15 pushed w_SPY>80%). Confirms K687: no VT beats BH 50/50 in Sharpe with correct lag. PART D — Competing signals: GFC era is the ONLY period where all 3 signals add value (overnight VIX t=-3.15, VRP t=-6.51, vol momentum t=7.60). Vol momentum also significant in COVID era (t=9.30). Normal eras: ZERO competing signals pass Harvey t>3.0. IMPLICATION: VIX sufficiency is the norm; crisis periods briefly open a window where additional signals (VRP, vol momentum) add tiny incremental R² (0.4-3.7%), but these are too small and too rare to be tradeable. KEY FINDING: VIX sufficiency is NOT a recent artifact — it holds from the 1993 VIX inception through 2026, across dot-com, GFC, QE, and COVID eras.

title: Paper 5 Plan: 'Can Anything Beat VIX?' — Codex evaluation + journal targets
content: [提出: Codex GPT-5.4, 執行: Claude] Paper 5 feasibility confirmed by Codex. Title: 'Can Anything Beat VIX? A Systematic OOS Evaluation of 11 Signal Families'. Journals: J. Forecasting (realistic), Int'l J. Forecasting (ambitious), Finance Research Letters (short). Key requirements: (1) uniform pipeline across all 11 families, (2) benchmark suite = VIX + HAR-RV + GARCH, (3) multiple-testing control (Bonferroni/Romano-Wolf), (4) subsample/regime robustness (K752), (5) replication package. Main reviewer attacks: HARKing, low power, signal not tuned as carefully as benchmark, US-specific. Outline: 9 sections. Need K752 era stability + cross-country validation for strongest version.

title: K753: Market Liquidity as Volatility Predictor — Volume has small partial corr but NO strategy value
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] SPY volume as vol predictor (2006-2026, N=5090). Part A: Volume-|ret| contemporaneous corr=0.333 (MDH confirmed), monotonic quintile pattern (Q1 0.50% → Q5 1.25%). Part B: Partial corr(volume→next |ret| | VIX)=0.089 (p<0.001) — statistically significant but economically tiny. Incremental R²=0.005 beyond VIX (0.325→0.331). DM test marginal (p=0.045). Volume change has zero predictive power (r=-0.009). Part C: "Calm before storm" NOT confirmed — volume drop → VIX spike lift only 1.19x (not actionable). Counterintuitively, EXTREME volume days have LOWEST subsequent VIX spike probability (12.6% vs 21% unconditional) — volume exhaustion effect. Part D: Volume strategy Sharpe 0.581 vs 12/VIX 0.729 vs 50/50 0.918 — volume strategy is WORST. Volume+VIX combo (0.626) also worse than VIX alone. Part E: Granger F-test not significant (p=0.132). Conclusion: Volume is a contemporaneous correlate of volatility (MDH) but VIX already prices this information. The tiny partial correlation (0.089) cannot translate into trading value. Refs: Lamoureux & Lastrapes (1990), Gallant et al. (1992), K710.

title: K753 new direction: Volume Exhaustion Effect — extreme volume predicts LOWER future VIX
content: K753 found counterintuitive result: extreme volume days (>2x avg) have LOWEST subsequent VIX spike probability (12.6% vs 21% unconditional). This 'volume exhaustion' effect is opposite to 'calm before storm'. Could be exploitable: after extreme volume days, reduce hedging because VIX spike risk is lower. Needs dedicated experiment with proper OOS testing.

title: Codex Review K753: 1 HIGH (double-lag in Part D), NULL safe
content: [提出: Codex, 執行: Claude] K753 review: (1) HIGH: Part D shift(1) is double-lag — ret_next already puts t+1 return on month-end t, shifting again uses t-1 info. Extra one-month staleness. (2) MEDIUM: 50/50 baseline no TX. (3) LOW: TX single-leg OK for SPY/cash. NULL conclusion safe (extra lag makes strategy worse).

title: Taiwan VT Cross-Validation Holiday-Bug Fix — All 4 Findings Survive
content: [提出: Codex (K739 review), 執行: Claude] K739b fixes 2 HIGH bugs from Codex review: (1) union calendar ffill created synthetic zero returns on ~1150 mismatched holidays (22.6% of days), polluting RV and seasonality; (2) ghost trades on closed-market days. FIX: separate calendars per market, VIX mapped via asof-lookup (most recent prior US close), TX only on open days. RESULTS: All 4 findings SURVIVE the fix with minor numerical shifts. Test1 VIX sufficiency: R2=0.036 (unchanged), own_rv gain still <1%. Test2 allocation: 0050+SPY optimal 40/60 (unchanged), 0050+GLD 30/70 (unchanged). Test3 calendar: Sell-in-May still insignificant (p=0.87). Test4 rebalancing: daily still best (Sharpe 0.41 vs monthly 0.26). The holiday bug affected 22.6% of days but conclusions are robust because zero-return days were roughly symmetric and VIX is slow-moving. Key lesson: proper calendar handling is methodologically necessary but practical impact was small for these tests.

title: K754: Volume Exhaustion Effect — Extreme Volume Does NOT Predict Lower Future Vol (Resolves K753 Paradox)
content: [提出: Claude (from K753 finding), 執行: Claude] K753 found extreme volume days (>2x avg) have lowest VIX spike prob (12.6% vs 21%). K754 tests whether this means lower FUTURE volatility. RESULT: OPPOSITE — extreme volume is followed by 86.5% HIGHER 5d realized vol (t=6.01, p<0.001, Cohen d=0.75). The K753 spike probability was misleading because extreme volume already occurs DURING high-vol periods (mean VIX 25.6 vs 19.3), so VIX has already spiked. The mean-reversion of VIX (5d VIX change -2.40 vs +0.06, t=-4.30) explains the lower spike prob — VIX drops FROM the already-elevated level, not TO a lower level. Key findings: (1) 95 extreme days in 20 yrs (4.8/yr), 76% are down days, 35% cluster next-day; (2) Forward RV is HIGHER at all horizons (1d/5d/22d all +65-87%); (3) VIX DROPS after extreme vol (mean reversion), but future RV stays elevated; (4) No direction asymmetry (UP vs DOWN extreme → same fwd RV, t=-0.32); (5) Strategy: vol_exhaust_simple Sharpe 0.59 vs 12/VIX 0.60 — NO improvement (DM t=0.39); (6) Cross-OOS: wins only 1/5 periods; (7) Effect stable across all sub-periods (2006-2025). CONCLUSION: Volume exhaustion is real for VIX level (mean reversion) but NOT for realized vol. Extreme volume signals ongoing turbulence, not resolution. The K753 finding was a CONFOUND: low spike prob because VIX is already high, not because risk is low.

title: K746b: ★★ Bitcoin-VIX Crypto Fear Channel — FIXED Methodology Confirms Bidirectional Causality
content: [提出: Codex (K746 review), 執行: Claude] Codex 審查 K746 發現 2 個 HIGH bug：(1) Granger 用 backward 22d RV（overlapping），(2) Fisher z-test 比較 BTC-SPY return corr 而非 VIX-BTC_RV corr。K746b 修正後結果：**VIX → BTC vol Granger 因果仍顯著**（AIC-optimal lag=7, p=0.013），但弱於 benchmark VIX→SPY（F=739 vs F=2.89）。**BTC vol → VIX 更強**（AIC-opt lag=10, p=0.0002, F=14.8 at lag 1）——非對稱性得到確認。Fisher z-test 修正為 VIX-BTC_RV 相關：Pre-2021=0.172 → 2021+=0.290，z=-3.29, p=0.001（顯著增強）。Andrews (1993) sup-Wald 確認斷點在 2022-08-10（sup=162.5, p<0.01），非人為假設 2021。關鍵發現：BTC 恐慌→VIX 因果強於反向，且 coupling 在機構化後增強。Portfolio：5% BTC 靜態提升 Sharpe 1.06→1.28；VIX>25 條件式避險有效但 TX cost 抵消部分收益。數據：yfinance BTC-USD/SPY/GLD/VIX 2015-2026, n=2803。

title: Codex Review K746b: 1 HIGH (Granger target doc mismatch) + 1 MEDIUM (Andrews partial)
content: [提出: Codex, 執行: Claude] K746b review: (1) HIGH: Granger target is |r_t| with lagged VIX, not explicitly |r_{t+1}|. But statsmodels grangercausalitytests uses VAR where 'lagged X→current Y' IS equivalent to 'X_t→Y_{t+1}'. Documentation misleading but result likely correct. (2) MEDIUM: Andrews test is sup-Chow scan with hardcoded cutoffs, not full Hansen bootstrap. (3) LOW: AIC lag selection correct, Fisher z on right variable, no lookahead in portfolio. DIRECTION: Granger finding (BTC vol→VIX, p=0.0002) probably valid but needs explicit shift(1) for clarity in Paper 6.

title: K755: ★★★ FOMO Cooling Mechanism — Lock-5d best (+0.022 Sharpe vs 12/VIX), mean reversion confirmed but none beat BH 50/50
content: [提出: Claude (from K743 + research_program), 執行: Claude] K755: FOMO COOLING MECHANISM. Data: yfinance SPY/GLD/VIX 2007-2026 (4839 trading days). Part A: FOMO events (SPY >+2%) occur 8.3x/year (159 events, 3.3% of days). CRITICAL FINDING: next-1d mean return -0.319% (t=-2.07, p<0.05) — statistically significant mean reversion! Next-2d: -0.35% (t=-1.43, ns). Next-5d: -0.49% (t=-1.35, ns). But by day 20, +1.06% (t=1.86, marginal momentum). VIX regime matters: 67% of FOMO events occur at VIX>25 (crisis recoveries, not genuine rallies). High-VIX FOMO next-5d: -0.83%; Low-VIX FOMO: +0.23%. Part B: 4 cooling variants vs perfect 12/VIX (Sharpe 0.505). Lock-5d BEST: Sharpe 0.527 (+0.022), MDD -0.312 (from -0.323). Lock-48h: 0.524. Gradual-return: 0.526. Cap-increase: 0.505 (≈no change). Combined Robust (Lock+Panic floor): 0.524, best MDD -0.306. Bootstrap: Lock-48h vs 12/VIX p=0.057, marginal significance. ALL cooling variants improve vs 12/VIX but NONE beat BH 50/50 (0.547). Sub-periods: cooling helps most during GFC (0.072→0.136 Sharpe) and recovery periods. Sensitivity: 1.5% threshold best Sharpe 0.531, MDD -0.298. Lock=10d hurts (0.494). CONCLUSION: FOMO cooling is a real but small effect (+2-4% Sharpe improvement over 12/VIX). Mean reversion after large rallies is genuine (especially high-VIX days). Cooling reduces turnover 5-8% and MDD 1-2pp. As behavioral guardrail it works; as alpha source it's marginal. Consistent with K743 (FOMO costliest mistake) but the systematic cure is mild.
evidence: Next-1d mean: -0.319% (t=-2.07, p<0.05) — significant mean reversion
67% of FOMO events occur at VIX>25 (crisis recovery bounces)
BH 50/50 Sharpe: 0.547 — none beat passive benchmark

title: K756: ★★★ International VIX Sufficiency — VIX Predicts Vol for ALL 12 Global Markets
content:
[提出: Claude (Paper 5 review + research_program), 執行: Claude] K756: 國際 VIX 充分性測試。12 個市場（SPY, EFA, EWG, EWU, EWJ, EWT, EWY, EWH, EEM, EWZ, GLD, USO）× 3 個模型（VIX-only, OwnRV-only, Combined）。2010-2026, 4040 obs per market。

**核心發現：VIX 是全球波動率預測指標。** 12/12 市場 VIX 都顯著預測 forward RV（全部通過 Harvey t>3.0）。R² 範圍 0.10（GLD）到 0.35（EWG），non-US 平均 R²=0.236（vs SPY 0.332）。歐洲最強（mean R²=0.324）、亞洲中等（0.212）、新興/商品最弱（0.177-0.209）。

**VIX 獨特貢獻（beyond own RV）**：12/12 市場 VIX 都提供 incremental R²（ΔR² 2.4%-9.3%），partial correlation 全部 Harvey 顯著（t=11.3-23.4）。EWU（UK）ΔR²=9.3% 最高，EWZ（Brazil）ΔR²=2.4% 最低。

**Cross-sectional 發現**：US-correlation 預測 VIX R²（Spearman r=0.773, p=0.005）。與美國市場越相關的市場，VIX 預測力越強。GLD 因為與 SPY 幾乎不相關（ρ=0.055），VIX R² 最低（0.10）。

**Region hierarchy**：Europe (0.324) > Americas (0.332) > Asia (0.212) > Emerging (0.209) > Commodity (0.177)。

**Paper 5 意義**：直接回應 reviewer「US-specific」質疑——VIX sufficiency 不限美國市場。data_source: yfinance (12 ETFs + ^VIX) data_period: 2010-2026 n_obs: 4040/market
data_source: yfinance (SPY, EFA, EWG, EWU, EWJ, EWT, EWY, EWH, EEM, EWZ, GLD, USO, ^VIX)

title: Taiwan CoVaR Contagion Structure: 0050→TSMC→Financial Sector
content: [提出: Claude(research_program), 執行: Claude] K757: Taiwan CoVaR contagion analysis (0050/TSMC/Fubon/Cathay, 2010-2026, N=3835). Part A: 0050-TSMC return corr=0.588, rolling 60d mean=0.811. Crisis (VIX>30) corr jumps to 0.910 vs calm 0.452 (+0.458 shift). Fubon-Cathay strongly coupled (0.772). Part B: Granger causality surprises — Financials lead TSMC (Fubon→TSMC F=6.11 p<0.001), not the reverse. Cathay→0050 significant (F=2.69, p=0.045). TSMC does NOT Granger-cause 0050 (confirming T16). Part C: CoVaR — TSMC β=0.102 significant (p=0.0006) for 0050 left-tail risk; Fubon/Cathay not significant (p>0.09). ΔCoVaR time trend near-significant (p=0.063), peaked 2020-2023. Part D: TSMC RV does NOT improve OOS prediction beyond VIX (R² 0.0251→0.0250). High partial corr TSMC_RV|VIX=0.515 is in-sample co-movement, not predictive. Conclusion: Taiwan contagion flows Financial→TSMC→0050(tail risk), but VIX alone is sufficient for VT. TSMC is a systemic risk contributor but not a leading indicator.

title: K758: Taiwan Investor Cross-Border Hedging — Practical Guide with Real Costs
content: [提出: Claude (research_program I7), 執行: Claude] K758: Comprehensive analysis of FX hedging for Taiwan investors holding US equities. Data: SPY, 0050.TW, GLD, USDTWD=X, ^TNX 2010-2026 (4003 obs after cleaning yfinance FX corruption). KEY FINDINGS: (1) FX adds only 2.6pp to SPY vol (17.1%→19.7%); FX accounts for 24% of SPY(TWD) variance. (2) SPY-FX correlation near zero (0.002) but USD strengthens modestly in crashes (+1.4% annualized on worst 5% SPY days) — weak natural hedge. (3) Specific crises: 2022 rate hike USD/TWD +14.9% cushioned SPY -24.5% to only -13.3% in TWD; COVID was neutral (+0.7%). (4) Full FX hedging costs 4.9%/yr retail (IR diff 1.1% + NDF spreads 3.6% + margin 0.12%), 1.9%/yr institutional. (5) Hedging HURTS Sharpe: unhedged SPY 0.801 vs hedged 0.736 (cost > benefit). (6) Best portfolio: 40% 0050 + 30% SPY + 30% GLD with 50% hedge → Sharpe 0.963, but even 0% hedge version scores 0.937. (7) Grid search 330 combos: optimal allocation robust at 30-50% 0050 + 20-40% SPY + 20-40% GLD. (8) Sub-period: 33/33/33 most stable across all 4 periods; hedging helps in low-rate eras, hurts in USD appreciation eras. (9) Practical rec for retail TW investors: 40% 0050 + 30% SPY + 30% GLD, NO FX hedge — too expensive. Confirms R14's 'do not hedge' conclusion with much more granular cost analysis. LIMITATIONS: yfinance FX data has corruption (cleaned), TNX as US rate proxy imperfect, TW deposit rate assumed flat 1.5%, NDF spreads are estimates.

title: K760: Alt Risk Premia Rotation NULL — Multi-factor vol strategies (variance carry + skew + equity + safe haven) all underperform 12/VIX
content: [提出: Codex (7th suggestion), 執行: Claude] K760: ALTERNATIVE RISK PREMIA ROTATION. Data: yfinance SPY/GLD/VIX/VIX3M 2007-2026 (4840 days). Hypothesis: harvesting 4 vol risk premia (variance carry, skew/term structure, equity, safe haven) and rotating by VIX regime can beat 12/VIX. 4 signals: (1) Variance Carry = (VIX-RV22d)/VIX mean=0.241 (2) Term Structure = max(0, 1-VIX/VIX3M) mean=0.099 (3) Equity = 12/VIX mean=0.682 (4) Safe Haven = 1-equity. 3 regimes: Low VIX<15 (32%), Normal 15-25 (50%), High >25 (18%). 3 strategies tested: Equal-Weight (Sharpe 0.762), Regime-Rotated (0.712), Carry-Weighted (0.773) — ALL below 12/VIX (0.829) and 50/50 (0.788). DM tests: all NS (p>0.75). Cross-OOS: 0-1/5 periods beat 50/50. KEY INSIGHT: variance carry and term structure signals are tiny (mean 0.24 and 0.10) vs 12/VIX (0.68) — averaging them dilutes the equity signal, reducing SPY allocation from 68% to 34%. This is effectively a MORE CONSERVATIVE portfolio, not a smarter one. VRP analysis: VIX>RV 84% of days (mean premium 3.6%), SPY returns +14%/yr when VRP>0 vs -1.9%/yr when VRP<=0, but t=1.29 (NS). Sensitivity: ±20% threshold change only ±3.8% Sharpe change (stable but still loses). COMMON_START 2023-2026: multi-premia Sharpe 1.90-1.94 vs 12/VIX 1.73, but 50/50 still best at 2.01. Confirms K175 (rotation adds noise) and T13 (VIX term structure no incremental value for VT). The fundamental problem: mixing 4 weak-to-moderate signals doesn't create a strong signal — it creates signal dilution. 12/VIX's simplicity IS its strength.

Multi-premia avg SPY weight 0.34 vs 12/VIX 0.68 — signal dilution

title: K763: Regime-Switched Carry Filter — Underperforms (Sharpe 0.674 vs 12/VIX 0.827)
content: [提出: Codex (7th suggestion), 執行: Claude] K763: Binary admission filter for vol risk premium harvesting. 3 filters: (1) term structure VIX/VIX3M<0.95, (2) VIX 5d momentum<0, (3) VIX level<30. Declining VIX=recovery where SPY returns highest (14.3% ann when defensive vs 8.9% risk-on). Filter is ANTI-correlated with best SPY periods. (2) Term structure alone (0.800) > all-3 combined (0.674) — complexity destroys value. (3) Simple VIX<20 (0.793) > carry filter. (4) TX 52 turns/yr (3x 12/VIX 16/yr) — binary switching=excessive churn. (5) Conservative variant (70/30 vs 40/60) best at 0.750 but still < 12/VIX. Confirms K760 (signal dilution), K161 (TS absorbed by VIX), K440 (VRP null). Smooth weighting dominates discrete regime switch. Script: experiments/k763_regime_carry_filter.py

title: K765: Explainable AI for Volatility — Which Features Matter Most?
content: [提出: Claude (research_program), 執行: Claude] K765 XAI for vol forecasting. 4-part analysis using SPY 2006-2026 (5090 obs). PART A: GJR-GARCH parameter importance. alpha is MOST VARIABLE (CV=0.972), beta MOST STABLE (CV=0.104). gamma does NOT predict forecast accuracy (t=-0.260, p=0.80, corr=-0.04). Persistence mean=0.956, range [0.782, 1.095]. PART B: HAR-ABS feature importance. WEEKLY horizon dominates (51.0%) >> monthly (39.2%) >> daily (9.8%). Daily beta is NEGATIVE (-0.107) — contrarian signal. VIX regime CHANGES feature importance: high VIX → weekly importance rises (0.59 vs 0.51, t=10.3), monthly drops (0.35 vs 0.48, t=-9.9). R²=0.298. PART C: SHAP-like decomposition (2020-2026, 1567 days). Monthly component is MOST crisis-sensitive (1.97x increase during high VIX vs calm). Weekly still largest absolute contributor (57.8% of total deviation). PART D: Component agreement as confidence indicator. Statistical: disagreement-error corr r=0.045 (p=0.007). But PRACTICAL value near zero — only 0.5% error reduction. Quintile monotonicity holds but effect too small. KEY INSIGHT: HAR-ABS works because WEEKLY horizon captures the 'goldilocks' timescale — not too noisy (daily) nor too sluggish (monthly). During crises, monthly component surges but weekly stays dominant. This explains WHY HAR beats GARCH: multi-scale structure adapts to regime. Script: experiments/k765_xai_volatility.py

title: K768: Conformal VaR Wrapper — Model-Agnostic Tail Risk Calibration
content: [提出: 文獻搜尋 arXiv:2602.03903, 執行: Claude] Conformal VaR calibration: model-agnostic post-hoc wrapper that adjusts any VaR forecast using expanding-window quantile of past (loss - VaR) residuals. SPY Normal 1% VaR: uncalibrated violation ratio 2.06x (Kupiec FAIL, Basel RED) → uniform conformal 1.24x (Kupiec PASS, Basel GREEN, 77% improvement). Three methods tested: (1) uniform quantile: simplest, 77% improvement, (2) time-decay (lambda=0.01): 70% improvement, (3) regime-weighted (VIX kernel + time decay): 62% improvement but best sub-period adaptation (Volmageddon 2.39x→0.99x). Key asymmetry: conformal fixes under-coverage (Normal 2x→1.2x) but worsens already-conservative models (Student-t 0.85x→1.3x). Portfolio 50/50 SPY/GLD: Normal 2.06x→1.32x (RED→GREEN). 5% VaR: Student-t time-decay achieves near-perfect 1.00x ratio. Limitations: needs 250-day history, cannot fix violation clustering (independence), expanding window has regime inertia. Codex review fixed regime VIX lookahead bug (using lagged VIX for historical weights). OOS: 2016-2026, N=2576. Data: yfinance SPY/GLD/VIX.
evidence: SPY+GLD 2826 OOS VaR forecasts, 3 conformal methods, Kupiec+Christoffersen tests, 5 sub-periods, Codex-reviewed

title: K767: HAR-RV with 5-Day Realized Volatility — Multi-Horizon, Cross-Asset (No Intraday Data)
content: [提出: 用戶, 執行: Claude] HAR-RV using daily-frequency multi-scale RV (5d/22d/66d squared returns sum) across SPY/GLD/0050.TW, 3 horizons (5d/22d/66d), expanding window OOS (2008-2026, N≈3600-4500). KEY RESULTS: (1) log-HAR dominates at longer horizons — best for GLD all 3 horizons and 0050.TW 22d+66d. Log specification avoids OLS negativity issues. (2) For SPY: GJR-GARCH wins 5d (QLIKE=0.464), VIX-implied wins 22d (0.387), HAR-5d+22d wins 66d (0.443). Different horizons favor different models. (3) HAR-full beats GARCH in 5/9 (56%) asset-horizon pairs — multi-scale helps. (4) Predictability increases with horizon for non-SPY: GLD R²_OOS 0.22→0.30→0.30; 0050.TW 0.05→0.09→0.10. (5) Only 5/57 DM tests pass Harvey t>3.0 — most model differences NOT significant. (6) 0050.TW much harder to forecast than SPY/GLD. (7) Daily-frequency RV works well — no intraday data needed for medium-horizon forecasting. Data: yfinance 2006-2026. 0050.TW had 1 data artifact removed (2014-01-02: -138.9% return from unadjusted split).

[提出: Gemini 2.5 Pro, 執行: Claude] K769: Transfer Entropy VT Budgeting — Dynamic Insurance Scaling via Information Flow. Tested whether TE(macro-liquidity → VIX) can scale VT insurance allocation. 6 FRED macro proxies (WALCL, EFFR, HY spread, yield slope, STLFSI2, DGS10) → composite TE signal. RESULT: NULL — all 3 TE-VT variants WORSE than static 12/VIX (Sharpe: TE_VT 0.739, TE_VT_AGG 0.702, TE_BINARY 0.748 vs 12/VIX 0.782 vs BH 50/50 0.847). TE scaling REDUCES equity weight too aggressively (avg SPY weight: 12/VIX=0.371, TE_VT=0.290, TE_VT_AGG=0.241) without compensating upside. TE-VIX correlation=0.289 — TE is HIGHER during high VIX (TE pctl 0.651 when VIX≥25 vs 0.405 when VIX<15), meaning TE reduces insurance precisely when it's most needed (crisis = more predictable = reduce insurance = BAD). Cross-OOS: all strategies win 2/7 periods vs BH. DM test: TE_VT significantly WORSE than 12/VIX (t=-2.40, p=0.017). Sensitivity: larger TE scalar = worse Sharpe (0.3→0.758, 0.5→0.739, 0.7→0.715). Conclusion: Gemini's hypothesis inverted — high TE during crises means 'reduce insurance during crisis' which is exactly wrong. VIX already encodes macro liquidity info. K152 confirmed again.

title: K772 Overnight Vol Decomposition: overnight=36.8%, HAR-OC insignificant, AMEM>GJR>HAR-OC
content: [提出: 用戶, 執行: Claude] K772: Hansen & Lunde (2005) overnight/intraday decomposition for SPY (2007-2026, n=4840). Part A: Overnight variance share = 36.8% of total (Hansen & Lunde benchmark ~20% — difference because they used 2000-era data with less overnight trading). Corr(overnight, intraday) = 0.040 (near-independent). Part B: Overnight share ranges 20-61% across years (2020 COVID peak 52.8%, 2018 low 25.1%). Regime-dependent: high-vol periods have slightly higher overnight share (37.9% vs 32.7% in low-vol). Part C: HAR-OC regression adds r²_overnight to HAR-RV². Overnight coefficient β₄=0.147, t=1.46 — NOT significant at Harvey |t|>3.0 threshold. R² improvement only 0.14% (0.2232→0.2248). The overnight squared return adds negligible predictive power beyond what weekly/monthly averages already capture. Part D: Expanding window OOS (n=3828, 2010-2026). QLIKE ranking: AMEM (1.507) > GJR (1.538) > HAR-OC (1.605) > EWMA (1.624) > HAR-RV² (1.673). HAR-OC-Ext overfits (QLIKE=162893). DM tests: AMEM beats all at p<0.05 (Harvey PASS vs EWMA/HAR-RV²/HAR-OC, FAIL vs GJR at p=0.035). GJR beats HAR-OC (DM=-6.62, Harvey PASS). HAR-OC vs HAR-RV²: DM=1.76, p=0.078 (marginal, Harvey FAIL). KEY INSIGHT: Overnight component is descriptively important (37% of variance) but has near-zero incremental PREDICTIVE power for next-day volatility. GARCH/AMEM already capture overnight info through close-to-close returns. Explicitly separating overnight adds nothing.

title: K776 DMEM (Long/Short Components): AMEM still wins — explicit decomposition loses OOS
content: [提出: 用戶 + 文獻, 執行: Claude] DMEM decomposes x_t = τ_t × g_t × ε_t into long-run τ_t = exp(ω_τ + α_τ × log(RV_22d)) and short-run g_t with leverage (7 params total). On SPY 2007-2026 (n_oos=4326), QLIKE ranking: AMEM(0.473) > DMEM(0.483) > GJR(0.487) > MEM(0.498) > HAR-ABS(0.502). DM test DMEM vs AMEM: +4.35 (Harvey PASS) — AMEM significantly better. Full-sample NLL improvement +122 (DMEM wins IS with 7 vs 5 params), but OOS the extra parameters hurt. α_g collapsed to 0 in DMEM (short-run ARCH dead). Regime split: DMEM wins calm (QLIKE 1.18 vs 1.22) but loses crisis (0.41 vs 0.37) — τ_t estimation noise amplified during volatility spikes. AMEM β=0.88 implicitly captures long-memory without explicit decomposition. Subsample: AMEM #1 in all 3 splits. Conclusion: simpler AMEM dominates despite DMEM theoretical appeal.

title: Patton (2011): QLIKE/MSE only rank correctly if proxy is conditionally unbiased for true vol
content: [提出: 文獻搜尋] Patton (2011, J. Econometrics) proved MSE and QLIKE are 'robust' loss functions — ranking is preserved even with noisy proxy, BUT only if proxy is conditionally unbiased estimator of true volatility. |r| is NOT unbiased for σ² (E[|r|] = σ×sqrt(2/π) under Normal, different under fat tails). r² IS unbiased for σ² (E[r²] = σ²). This means: (1) comparing models on QLIKE(|r|) favors models that predict |r| natively, (2) comparing on QLIKE(r²) favors σ² models, (3) rank correlation (Spearman) is distribution-free and avoids this problem entirely. K777 addresses this by doing all three.

title: Literature: Fair volatility model comparison framework (Hansen&Lunde 2005, Patton 2011, MCS)
content: [提出: 用戶 + 文獻搜尋] Academic best practice for fair vol model comparison: (1) Hansen&Lunde 2005: r² as proxy severely distorts ranking, use 5-min RV instead. (2) Patton 2011: QLIKE is proxy-robust IF proxy is conditionally unbiased for σ². r² IS unbiased (E[r²]=σ²), |r| is NOT. So QLIKE on r² is correct, QLIKE on |r| is biased. (3) Patton&Sheppard 2009: QLIKE has more power than MSE on r² proxy. (4) Hansen,Lunde&Nason 2011: MCS for multi-model comparison without data snooping. (5) Economic evaluation: use portfolio Sharpe/utility, not just forecast accuracy. Our K777 should primarily use QLIKE on r² (not |r|) + Spearman (distribution-free) + MCS.

title: K780: Tail-First ES Allocation — AMEM Best Risk Manager, ES-alloc beats 50/50 by +0.06 Sharpe

(2) GJR-GARCH 2nd (1.63): good at 5% but slightly over-violates at 1%. (3) HAR-ABS/EWMA worst: Gaussian tails too thin → 2.5x over-violation at 1%, Basel Yellow. (6) All Acerbi-Szekely ES tests passed (p>0.5) — ES conservatively calibrated. Data: yfinance SPY/GLD/VIX 2006-2026, expanding window, 73 refits.

title: K783c: Cross-Period Window Size Sensitivity (GJR-GARCH, SPY, 3 Regimes)
content:
[提出: 用戶, 執行: Claude] K783c 驗證 GJR-GARCH(1,1) 訓練視窗大小是否依市場 regime 不同而有差異。三個不重疊 OOS 期間（各 ~500 天）：高波動（2020-2021 COVID 崩潰+復甦）、中等（2018-2019 貿易戰/Fed pivot）、平靜（2016-2017 低 VIX 時代）。視窗：{252, 504, 1000, 2000, 3000, ALL}，指標：QLIKE on r²（Patton 2011）。
核心發現：最佳視窗確實因 regime 不同而改變——高波動期(2020-21): w=2000 勝（vs w=252 +63%, w=504 +23%）；中等波動期(2018-19): w=504 勝（vs w=2000 +9.4%），w=1000 是唯一通過 Harvey t>3.0 門檻的 DM 檢定（t=-3.077）；平靜期(2016-17): w=252 勝（vs w=2000 +12.7%），但無一通過 Harvey 門檻。
統計意義：只有 1 個 DM test 通過 Harvey t>3.0（w=1000 vs w=2000 在 2018-19，t=-3.077）。其餘 14 個比較均未達顯著差異。
詮釋：大視窗（2000+）在危機期表現好（需要長期歷史估計尾部分布），中小視窗（252-504）在平靜/中等期表現好（快速適應低波動環境）。但差異在統計上多不顯著，與 K783 結論一致：視窗選擇對預測品質影響相對有限。
建議：危機敏感應用用 w=2000，平時用 w=504 是合理折衷（兩個極端 regime 表現都不差）。

title: K792: EWT vs 0050.TW Volatility Spread Signal — Granger Causality, Lead-Lag, Predictive Regression
content:
[提出: User, 執行: Claude] K792 深度分析 EWT（美掛台灣 ETF）與 0050.TW 的波動率差異訊號，探討 vol_ratio = RV_22d(EWT)/RV_22d(0050) 是否具有預測力。數據：2012-2025，3393 個交易日，0050.TW 以 clean_tw50_data 修正股分拆偽影。
核心發現：
1. Granger 因果：vol_ratio 對 rv_tw50 具高度顯著 Granger 因果（lag=1~22，F≥5.78，p<0.0001）。rv_ewt 直接預測 rv_tw50 效果更強（lag=1 F=35.3，p<0.0001）。但反向（rv_tw50→vol_ratio）也顯著（lag=1 F=4.2，p=0.04），代表是雙向回饋而非純粹單向因果。
2. 預測迴歸（vol_ratio[t-1] → rv_tw50[t]）：β=-0.0894，t=-20.1（高度顯著）R²=0.107。方向為負——高 vol_ratio 時 0050 波動反而降低。解讀：當 EWT 相對於 0050 波動率較高，代表美國交易者已消化了風險、台灣本地市場趨於平靜（或有均值回歸）。
3. rv_ewt[t-1] → rv_tw50[t]：β=+0.728，R²=0.671（極強共動性）——EWT 與 0050 波動率本身高度同步（同期相關 0.82）。
4. vol_ratio[t-1] → tw50_ret[t]：β=-0.001194，t=-1.67，p=0.096（統計不顯著）——vol_ratio 不能預測 0050 日報酬。符合 K697（VIX 預測波動量但不預測方向）的既有結論。
5. 策略：以 vol_ratio>1.3 減半 VT 權重（signal.shift(1) 確保無前視偏誤），Sharpe=1.346，低於純 VT 1.502。結論：vol_ratio 訊號對 0050 有波動率預測力但無報酬方向預測力，用它作為 VT overlay 會損害績效。
延伸：與 K506（EWT vol spread 為 VT overlay，2/5 OOS FAIL）一致——訊號有統計意義但非交易可利用。EWT vol ratio 是很好的「何時波動率將下降」訊號，但不是報酬訊號。

title: K798: Decision-Focused Policy Learning — All 3 approaches fail Harvey t>3.0 vs 12/VIX. SPY bull 2023-25 dominated.
content:
[提出: Codex, 執行: Claude] K798 tests whether decision-focused learning (skip prediction, directly optimize action) can beat standard 12/VIX on SPY+GLD. Three approaches tested on OOS 2023-2025 (n=751).

核心發現:
1. DF-OLS (Mean-Variance direct): OOS Sharpe=2.196 vs 12/VIX 1.509 (+0.687), but DM t=-0.687 (p=0.49) — NOT significant. Mean weight=0.545 (near static 50/50).
2. FC-Policy (OLS features→optimal_w): OOS Sharpe=2.262, MDD=-7.9% (best MDD). DM t=-0.924 (p=0.36) — NOT significant. Mean weight=0.641 (overweight SPY in bull market).
3. Contextual Bandit (ε=0.1, 6 arms, 5 VIX contexts): OOS Sharpe=2.008. DM t=-0.171 (p=0.86) — NOT significant.
4. BH 50/50 wins CRRA utility (gamma=5): -0.249100 vs all adaptive strategies.
5. Harvey t>3.0 breaches: 0/5 DM tests. None significant.

關鍵洞見:
- All decision-focused methods appear better on Sharpe in 2023-2025 OOS, but this reflects a bull SPY market (S&P up ~70% in 2023-25) — methods that overweight SPY win trivially.
- DF-OLS converges to mean_w=0.545 (nearly static), essentially a slight SPY tilt.
- FC-Policy mean_w=0.641 is significantly overweighted in SPY — would lose in bear market.
- Bandit learned contradictory policy: Q1 (low VIX) → arm=0.8, Q3 (medium VIX) → arm=0.2 (reduces SPY in medium VIX). Inconsistent.
- No method passes Harvey t>3.0. 12/VIX irreducible result #7 (following K440/K470/K488/K524).
- Conclusion: Decision-focused approaches do NOT provide statistically significant improvement over 12/VIX. Sample period (strong bull) creates misleading Sharpe numbers.

數據來源: yfinance SPY/GLD/VIX 2007-2025, OOS 2023-01-03 to 2025-12-30 (n=751)

title: K801: VIX Shock Guard — Event-Surprise Strategy NULL
content: [提出: Codex #5, 執行: Claude] K801 tests whether VIX daily change > 2σ (rolling 252d) can improve the 12/VIX strategy by reducing equity exposure for 5 days after large VIX shocks (surprise proxy). Four variants tested: (A) 50% weight reduction after any shock, (B) go to cash after any shock, (C) reduce only on spikes (ΔVIX > +2σ), (D) boost to 100% after drops. Data: SPY+VIX yfinance 2010-2025, N=3960, OOS=2023-2025 N=751. Shock frequency: 4.8% of days (192 events). Guard active: 15.6% of days. Results — Full period: Baseline Sharpe=0.813, Guard=0.818, Binary=0.763, Spike=0.816, Drop-Boost=0.615. DM t-stats all near zero (range -1.2 to -0.06, none |t|>3). OOS: all variants Sharpe 1.28-1.50 vs baseline 1.41 — no consistent improvement. Forward return analysis: post-shock 5d SPY returns indistinguishable from zero (t=0.29, p=0.77); normal days clearly positive (t=8.42, p<0.001). CONCLUSION: NULL. VIX shock guard adds no independent signal beyond 12/VIX. VIX LEVEL already encodes recent surprise via mean-reversion dynamics; daily change carries no incremental predictive power. Consistent with K498 (calendar dummies also null).

title: K802: GJR + Skewed-t VaR — Dual Champion Achieved
content:
[提出: 用戶, 執行: Claude]

K802 resolves the K799 conflict: GJR wins QLIKE but fails VaR 1% under Normal distribution assumption. By replacing the Normal quantile with a fat-tail distribution, GJR achieves BOTH best QLIKE and VaR Trinity PASS simultaneously.

KEY RESULTS (SPY 2023-2024, n=502 OOS days):
- QLIKE: GJR=1.4686 vs GARCH=1.5137 (GJR wins, DM t=-3.25, p=0.001, Harvey t>3.0 PASS)
- Spearman: GJR rho=0.2116 >> GARCH rho=0.1087

VaR BACKTEST (1% level, Trinity = Kupiec + Christoffersen + Basel Green):
- GJR+Normal: violations=9/502 (1.79%), Kupiec p=0.108 → Basel YELLOW → FAIL (replicates K799)
- GJR+StudentT: violations=6/502 (1.20%), all PASS → Trinity PASS
- GJR+SkewedT: violations=6/502 (1.20%), all PASS → Trinity PASS ← DUAL CHAMPION
- GARCH+Normal: violations=7/502 (1.39%), all PASS → Trinity PASS (K799 baseline)
- GJR+FHS: violations=5/502 (1.00%), Kupiec p=0.993 → Trinity PASS

DISTRIBUTION PARAMETERS (estimated from IS standardized residuals):
- Student-t df ≈ 15–16 (fat tails, not ~5 as often assumed)
- Skewed-t xi ≈ 0.99 (nearly symmetric — equity returns in 2023-2024 not strongly skewed)
- FHS 1% quantile ≈ -2.73 to -2.81 (vs Normal -2.33, confirming fat tails)

CONCLUSION: GJR+Skewed-t is the Dual Champion — best σ² forecasting (QLIKE) AND correct VaR tail coverage. The Normal distribution underestimates tails (z=-2.33 too small), while Student-t df~16 and Skewed-t both give z~-2.58 to -2.60, achieving correct 1% VaR coverage. The high df (15-16) means tails are fatter than Normal but not as extreme as often parameterized (df=5). Xi~0.99 (near-symmetric) in the 2023-2024 period.

title: K803: VIX Term Structure Overlay NULL for 12/VIX Strategy
content: [提出: User, 執行: Claude] K803 測試 VIX3M/VIX 期限結構比率作為 12/VIX 策略的覆蓋信號。3 個變體：(1) Contango Guard：VIX3M/VIX<0.95 時 weight×0.5；(2) Contango Smooth：weight×min(1, VIX3M/VIX)；(3) Contango Binary：VIX3M/VIX<0.90 時現金 5 天。數據：SPY+^VIX+^VIX3M yfinance 2008-2026，N=4588。全期 Sharpe：Baseline=0.641, Guard=0.684, Smooth=0.649, Binary=0.703。OOS(2023-2024) Sharpe：Baseline=1.194, Guard=1.206, Smooth=1.192, Binary=1.100。HAC NW return-spread t-stats：Guard t=+0.48(NS), Smooth t=-0.25(NS), Binary t=+0.38(NS)，全部低於 Harvey t>3.0 門檻。Term structure 特性：backwardation(VIX3M/VIX<1) 佔 10.4%，backwardation 日 SPY 均報酬=-0.61%（高壓力），contango 日=+0.12%。Binary 策略降低全期 MDD 從 -23.7% 到 -16.4%，但 OOS MDD 反而更差（-12.9% vs -11.1%）。結論：NULL RESULT，第 4 次 VIX TS 覆蓋失敗（T13、N102、N177 皆失敗）。12/VIX 已隱含期限結構信息，額外信號不提供增量。

title: Cross-Asset GJR VaR Validation: Student-t fixes Normal tail underestimation on 3/4 assets
content: [提出: 用戶, 執行: Claude] K804 extends K802 (GJR+SkewedT dual champion on SPY) to 4 asset classes. OOS 2023-2024, expanding window, refit every 63 days. Results: GJR Normal VaR FAILS on 2/4 assets (QQQ 2.0% rate, 0050.TW 1.87% — both Basel YELLOW). Student-t VaR PASSES 3/4: QQQ df=8.2 (6 violations, green), GLD df=5.0 (3 violations), 0050.TW df=4.9 (6 violations). FHS (empirical quantile) also PASSES 3/4. The one exception is BTC-USD: Normal surprisingly over-conservative (3/731 violations, 0.41%), while Student-t df=3.2 and FHS are TOO conservative (1 violation each, 0.14%, Kupiec FAIL). BTC has positive skewness (+0.619) vs all equity assets (negative skew), suggesting fat-tail correction overshoots in crypto. QLIKE ranking by asset: SPY 1.469 < GLD 1.491 = QQQ 1.492 < 0050.TW 1.657 < BTC 1.984 — higher QLIKE = harder to predict, consistent with asset complexity. Key conclusion: Student-t distribution fixes GJR Normal tail underestimation for EQUITY assets (QQQ, GLD, 0050.TW: 3/3 fixed), but not for crypto where BTC has right-skewed returns and over-conservative VaR. Codex review caught 2 HIGH severity bugs pre-run: (1) Kupiec n1=0 falsely PASS, (2) Student-t quantile missing sqrt((df-2)/df) scale correction for unit-variance residuals.

key_numbers.btc_anomaly: right-skewed returns (+0.619), Normal over-conservative (0.41%), t and FHS too conservative (0.14%)
key_numbers.equity_finding: Student-t fixes Normal on all 3 equity/commodity assets

[提出: arXiv:2508.15922, 執行: Claude] K824 Quantile Forecasting — HistSim 冠軍

GJR-GARCH 標準化殘差的分位數預測。4 方法比較（SPY OOS 2023-2024, 502 obs）。

Pinball Loss 排名：
1. M4 HistSim: 0.001148（最佳，零參數假設）
2. M3 QuantReg: 0.001151
3. M1 Normal: 0.001152
4. M2 StudentT: 0.001152

VaR 1% Backtesting：
- Normal: 10 violations (2.0%) FAIL（Basel Yellow）
- StudentT: 8 violations (1.6%) FAIL（Basel Yellow）
- QuantReg: 4 violations (0.8%) PASS（Basel Green）
- HistSim: 4 violations (0.8%) PASS（Basel Green）

DM tests 全 NS（差異在第 6 位小數）。

結論：
1. Data-driven（HistSim/QuantReg）通過 VaR 1%，parametric（Normal/Student-t）失敗
2. GJR 點預測是核心（K802 確認），分位數方法只影響尾部校準
3. HistSim（零假設、簡單、快速）是最佳選擇——比 Student-t 更好
4. 更新最佳工具指南：VaR 應用 GJR + HistSim（非 GJR + Student-t）

結果數據: experiments/k824_quantile_forecasting_results.json

K824 Codex 審查：2 HIGH — HistSim 勝 Student-t 結論不可靠

HIGH 1: Student-t df 估計缺 scale term sqrt((df-2)/df)。z_t 是 unit-variance，但 t-dist fit 沒有 rescale。
df 偏向更薄的尾部 → Student-t VaR 被低估 → violations 被高估。修正後 Student-t 可能表現更好。

HIGH 2: Basel traffic light 是自定義（ad-hoc rate thresholds），非標準 Basel 測試。
Student-t 8/502 已通過 Kupiec (p=0.2185) 但被自定義規則標為 fail。

結論：K824 的 HistSim > Student-t 結論不可靠。需 K824v2 修正：
1. Student-t df 估計加入 scale term
2. 用標準 Basel traffic light（250 天回溯窗，Green<5, Yellow 5-9, Red≥10）
3. 修正後重新比較

暫時恢復 VaR 最佳實踐為 GJR + Student-t（K802 結論）。

[提出: arXiv:2508.15922, 執行: Claude] K824v2 Quantile Fixed — HistSim 確認勝 Student-t（乾淨結果）

修正 K824 的 2 HIGH bug 後重新比較。Student-t df 修正（scale term）+ 標準 Basel 250 天。

修正後結果（SPY OOS 2023-2024, 502 obs）：
1. HistSim: Pinball 0.001148, VaR 1% 4 violations (0.8%), Basel Green, Trinity PASS ★
2. QuantReg: 0.001149, 5 violations, Basel Yellow, FAIL
3. Normal: 0.001152, 7 violations, Basel Yellow, FAIL
4. Student-t: 0.001154, 5 violations, Basel Yellow, FAIL

Student-t df 修正後：mean=6.68 [6.25-7.09]（K824 未修正時偏高→薄尾→violations 被低估）
修正後 Student-t 仍 5 violations（Basel Yellow）→ HistSim 仍勝

DM tests 全 NS（pinball 差異在第 6 位小數）。

最終結論（K824v2 乾淨確認）：
- VaR 最佳實踐 = GJR + HistSim（零假設、Basel Green、唯一 Trinity PASS）
- Student-t 是次佳但 Basel Yellow
- GJR 點預測是核心，分位數方法決定合規性

K824v2 Codex：3 HIGH 但不影響 1% VaR 主結論

HIGH 1: Kupiec boundary auto-pass（0 or N violations → p=1.0）— 我們 4/5 violations 不在 boundary ✓
HIGH 2: Christoffersen boundary auto-pass — 同上 ✓
HIGH 3: 5% VaR 用 1% Basel 閾值 — 只影響 5% section，1% VaR 結論不受影響 ✓
MEDIUM: 應稱 FHS（Filtered Historical Simulation）非 plain HistSim — 命名修正

1% VaR 結論確認有效：FHS 4 violations (Basel Green) > Student-t 5 violations (Basel Yellow)。
Student-t scale term 修正正確。

但需注意：正確名稱應該是 GJR + FHS（不是 GJR + HistSim）。

title: K824v2: Quantile Forecasting Bug-Fixed — HistSim唯一Basel Green + Trinity PASS
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K824v2修正K824的兩個bug後(Student-t df scale term + Basel 250天窗口)重新驗證4種1% VaR方法。結果：HistSim 4/502 violations(0.80%), Basel Green, Trinity PASS——唯一通過所有檢驗的方法。Student-t 7/502(1.39%) Basel Yellow; Normal 9/502(1.79%) Basel Yellow; QuantReg 5/502(1.00%) Basel Yellow。DM tests全NS(Harvey t>3.0門檻)，但HistSim在實務標準(Basel+Trinity)上獨佔鰲頭。Avg pinball loss: HistSim 0.001148最佳但差異微小。結論：零假設方法(HistSim)勝過參數方法(Student-t/Normal)用於1% VaR。GJR+HistSim確認為VaR最佳實踐。Codex審查3 HIGH但均不影響1% VaR結論。

title: K824: Quantile Forecasting原始版 — 有兩個bug(Student-t scale + Basel窗口)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K824首次測試4種分位數方法的VaR表現。發現HistSim看似最佳但Student-t benchmark有bias(缺少df scale term sqrt((df-2)/df))，Basel窗口計算也有誤。結果不可靠，由K824v2修正後重跑。教訓：Student-t分配必須考慮scale term使標準化殘差unit variance。

title: K826: KAN-GARCH-MIDAS — ML ceiling第7次確認，KAN僅加0.06%改善
content: [提出: Claude (research_program.md), 執行: Claude] K826用Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks(B-spline, 71 params)替代GARCH-MIDAS的線性長期組件。GJR QLIKE -8.680勝KAN_MIDAS -8.582(DM t=-3.16 Harvey PASS)和Linear_MIDAS -8.577(DM t=-3.23 Harvey PASS)。KAN僅比Linear MIDAS改善0.06%(DM t=1.57 NS)。Regime分析：GJR在高/中/低波動期全勝。KAN偵測到顯著非線性(ratio=5.9%)但OOS無法轉化為預測改善。GJR Spearman 0.222 vs KAN 0.072(幾乎無序關係)。結論：ML ceiling第7次確認——結構化NN(KAN)也無法突破GJR的QLIKE優勢。長期vol組件(τ)僅解釋少量variance，GJR的短期遞迴已足夠。

title: K850: HAR-RV VaR台灣 — 悖論：HAR預測好54%但VaR更差，GJR+CF仍是冠軍
content: [提出: research_program.md, 執行: Claude] K850用TAIFEX 5-min RV的HAR-RV做0050.TW VaR。悖論發現：HAR QLIKE 0.101 vs GJR 0.220(好54%, DM t=-5.60)但1% VaR: HAR+CF 17/450 Red FAIL vs GJR+CF 2/481 Green PASS。原因：VaR取決於殘差尾部行為而非sigma精度。GJR的in-model標準化殘差捕捉尾部結構更好(CF修正後VaR -3.83% vs HAR -2.52%——GJR更保守52%)。5% VaR: HAR+HistSim Trinity PASS(26/450)。結論：vol prediction quality ≠ VaR quality。GJR+CF仍是0050.TW 1% VaR唯一冠軍。K849的HAR優勢限於預測精度，不延伸到風險管理。
data_source: TAIFEX TX tick 5-min RV + yfinance 0050.TW, OOS 2023-2025

title: K851: Jump Dynamics — Formal BNS Test Shows Only 10.1% Jump Days, No Significant OOS Improvement (DM t=1.10 NS)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K851 tests whether TAIFEX TX1 jump components (Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2004 bipower variation, formal z-test α=0.001) predict next-day RV in log-HAR framework. Data: 2,107 days (2017-2026 night session era), OOS: 633 days (2023-2026). CRITICAL FINDING: Formal BNS test reduces jump detection from naive 74.9% (K848) to only 10.1% — most apparent jumps are sampling noise. Jumps contribute only 2.5% of total RV. Jump AC(1)≈0, no clustering (ratio 1.13x). 4 models: HAR-RV (QLIKE 0.121), HAR-CJ (0.122, worse), HAR-CJ-A (0.116, +4.57% but DM t=1.10 NS), HAR-CJ-Night (0.127, worse). Night session=62.5% of jump variance. Continuous component R²=0.694 in log-space. All jump coefficients IS insignificant (max |t|=1.65). CONCLUSION: Consistent with ABD (2007) for US equities — separating jumps from continuous variation adds minimal forecasting value in HAR. The continuous component captures 97.5% of variance with strong long-memory. Negative jumps show suggestive but insignificant asymmetry. Taiwan futures conform to the international pattern.

title: K852: Realized GARCH — 部分解決K849/K850悖論，RGL+CF兩維度都好
content: [提出: K849衍生, 執行: Claude] K852用Realized GARCH結合RV測量和GARCH結構。RealGARCH-Log+CF：Trinity PASS(3 violations=GJR+CF)且Spearman 0.790(最佳rank ordering)。HAR仍是QLIKE冠軍(0.101 vs RGL 0.209)但RGL在兩個維度都top-3。GJR被RealGARCH-Simple超16% QLIKE(但DM t=1.91 NS)。關鍵insight：GARCH殘差結構(CF tail correction)對VaR至關重要——HAR殘差kurtosis 4.0太厚，violations過多。RealGARCH兩全其美：RV信息→更好預測，GARCH殘差→更好VaR。台灣vol模型最佳實踐更新：預測用HAR-RV，VaR用GJR+CF或RealGARCH-Log+CF，兩維度最佳=RealGARCH-Log+CF。
data_source: TAIFEX TX tick 5-min RV + yfinance 0050.TW, OOS 2023-2024

title: K853: Proxy Ceiling Ablation — HAR勝GJR即使在r²下(t=-5.14)，但r²壓縮優勢4倍
content: [提出: Codex adversarial H1, 執行: Claude] K853固定sample/window只改evaluation target做ablation。結果：(A) r²: HAR勝GJR DM t=-5.14(proxy不翻轉排名！)(B) RV_day: HAR勝 t=-11.14(66%優勢)(C) RV_total: GJR勝 t=+4.02(HAR只訓練day RV不含夜盤)。結論：proxy ceiling不是翻轉排名而是壓縮優勢——r²下HAR優勢16% vs RV_day下66%(4倍壓縮)。Paper 2需修正：從'proxy reverses rankings'改為'proxy severely mutes the signal'。Condition C反轉是target mismatch非proxy問題。
data_source: TAIFEX TX tick + yfinance 0050.TW, OOS 2020-2025 (1448 days)

title: K854: Common Sample VaR — Paradox CONFIRMED, 不是 sample artifact
content: [提出: Codex H2, 執行: Claude] K854統一450天OOS比較7模型。HAR QLIKE 0.100 vs GJR 0.205(DM t=-4.98好51%)但HAR VaR全FAIL(9-17 violations)。GJR+CF和RGL+CF都3 violations Trinity PASS。GJR+Skewed-t 9 violations FAIL。結論：prediction-VaR paradox不是sample truncation artifact而是genuine methodological difference——HAR殘差寬尾導致VaR校準差。Codex H2 resolved。
data_source: TAIFEX TX tick + yfinance 0050.TW, 450 common OOS days

title: K852b: Regime-Dependent HAR — Monthly Component Flips Sign at High VIX, but OOS NULL (DM all NS)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K852b tests whether HAR-RV coefficients change across VIX regimes for TAIFEX TX1. Data: 2,107 days (2017-2026), OOS: 843 days. STRUCTURAL FINDING: HAR coefficients are strongly regime-dependent. Daily beta rises 0.40→0.62 as VIX increases. Monthly beta FLIPS SIGN to -0.086 in high VIX (mean-reversion). ST-HAR (γ=0.05, c=25.7) confirms: low-VIX state is weekly+monthly dominated (long-memory), high-VIX state is daily-dominated (reactive). ST-HAR improves 21.5% in high-VIX subsample (QLIKE 0.299 vs 0.380) but only 75 days, DM t=1.56 NS. OOS overall: standard HAR-RV still best QLIKE (0.1187). No regime model passes Harvey. Consistent with K783c: regime structure is real but estimation noise offsets benefit. IMPLICATION FOR PAPER 2: the coefficient instability is a reportable structural finding even though it doesn't improve forecasting.

title: K855: Crypto Fear Channel Paradox — Granger Weakened Post-ETF but Shock Transmission 2.5x Larger
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K855 updates K746b's crypto fear channel with 2026 tariff crisis data (BTC/SPY/VIX, 2020-2026). PARADOX: Post-BTC-ETF (2024+), linear Granger causality BTC→VIX WEAKENED (p=0.32 vs pre-ETF p=0.005), but VAR impulse response shows shock transmission AMPLIFIED 2.5x (-6.50→-16.03 cumulative at day 10). Channel is now event-driven (nonlinear), not day-to-day predictable. BTC increasingly risk-on: rolling 60d corr(BTC,SPY)>0.3 in 76% of post-ETF days vs 57% pre-ETF, 100% during tariff crisis. BUT Fisher z-test shows no significant structural break (z=0.26, p=0.79) — shift is gradual. Asymmetric Granger still holds: BTC→VIX significant only in high-VIX regime (p=0.03). BTC NO LONGER a diversifier in traditional sense. Paper 6 angle: 'institutional adoption amplified shock transmission but destroyed linear predictability — a volatility contagion paradox.'

title: K856: Fed Rate Causal Inference — All 4 Methods NULL, VIX Anticipates (Not Reacts to) FOMC
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K856 applies causal inference (Event Study + RDD + DiD + Surprise Regression) to 220 FOMC meetings (2000-2026, 41 hikes/31 cuts/148 holds). ALL FOUR METHODS NULL: Event study p=0.97, RDD t=-1.12 p=0.26, DiD ATT=+1.16% t=0.48 p=0.63, Surprise beta=-0.24 t=-0.21. Regime transitions also NS (Fisher p=0.86). MOST INTERESTING: Anticipation test shows VIX rises +1.90 before cuts (t=1.62 marginal) and falls -0.75 before hikes (t=-1.91 marginal). Market pre-adjusts VIX, leaving no residual causal effect at announcement. Consistent with efficient markets and K185/K514. CONCLUSION: Fed rate decisions do NOT cause VIX regime shifts — VIX prices in FOMC outcomes beforehand. The 'causal' effect is actually an anticipation effect that occurs in the days leading up to the meeting.

title: K857: TSMC Revenue Vol 2026 Update — Event Day 1.23x Vol, VIX>30 Means 3.18% Absolute Move
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K857 updates K617 with 135 TSMC revenue events (2015-2026). Event day |ret| 0.999% vs 0.811% (1.23x, t=1.69 marginal p=0.093). REGIME INTERACTION: Low VIX event/pre ratio 1.53x, High VIX ratio 1.12x (baseline already elevated). VIX>=30 events (n=6): mean |ret|=3.18% (4x normal), includes extreme +9.99% (2025-04-10 tariff rebound). SURPRISE ASYMMETRY: positive surprises generate HIGHER vol (1.20% vs 0.79%) — good TSMC news moves markets more. TSMC amplification 2.18x vs 0050 (2.88x in high VIX). PREDICTION for April 10, 2026: if VIX stays >25, expect 0050 |ret| ~1.6-3.2%. Post-event vol crush pattern observed (1.19% post vs 1.42% pre in high VIX).

title: K858: Congressional Trading Alpha NULL — Aggregate Portfolio CAGR 10.83% vs SPY 11.45%, t=-0.15
content: [提出: 會員 ideahub.everything, 執行: Claude] K858 tests whether aggregate U.S. congressional stock trades generate alpha. Data: 13,401 trades (2020-2022), 165 House members, 2,061 tickers. STRATEGY: Monthly top-10 net-bought tickers (equal weight), using disclosure_date+1 (realistic, no lookahead). RESULT: CAGR 10.83% vs SPY 11.45% (-0.61%), Sharpe 0.502 vs 0.488, MDD -35.2% vs -36.2%. t-stat=-0.153 (p=0.879), far from Harvey 3.0. EVEN WITH PERFECT INFO (transaction_date+1): CAGR 10.07%, STILL underperforms. Disclosure lag median 27 days but is NOT the bottleneck. BUY/SELL ASYMMETRY: most-sold tickers (+11.41%) outperform most-bought (+10.83%) — aggregate buying is not a positive signal. Top traders: Gottheimer ($112M), DelBene ($99M), Pelosi ($80M). CONCLUSION: Aggregate congressional portfolio provides no alpha over SPY. Individual members (e.g., Pelosi) may have alpha but aggregation destroys it.

title: K859: Robust VT — Floor/Cap+EWMA(10) Best Combo, Sharpe 0.579, Turnover -30% vs Baseline
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K859 tests robust modifications to 12/VIX monthly VT. Data: SPY/GLD/VIX 2005-2026 (5094 days). All use shift(1). BEST COMBO: Floor(0.3)+Cap(0.9)+EWMA(10)+monthly = Sharpe 0.579 (baseline 0.566), turnover 0.96x (baseline 1.39x, -30%). Floor/Cap alone: +0.011 Sharpe, turnover 1.13x. EWMA(22): +0.007 Sharpe, turnover 0.92x. Weekly rebalance HURTS (-0.024 Sharpe, 3x turnover). Daily even worse. NO modification achieves Harvey t>3.0 — confirms K687: VT mods are marginal. Cross-OOS: all VT beat BH 50/50 in 3/5 periods. CRRA utility: VT dominates BH at all gamma. MDD: ~30% for all VT vs 55.2% for BH 50/50. PRACTICAL: Floor+Cap+EWMA(10-22)+monthly is the recommended robust VT — cheaper insurance (less turnover) for same protection.

title: K860: Prospect Theory Flips VT Evaluation — Loss Aversion λ=1.52 Makes Robust VT Preferred Over BH 50/50
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K860 evaluates VT strategies under Prospect Theory (Tversky & Kahneman 1992, α=β=0.88, λ=2.25). Data: SPY/GLD/VIX 2005-2026. KEY FINDING: PT reverses VT evaluation. Sharpe says BH 50/50 (0.587) > VT Robust (0.579), but PT CE says VT Robust (-0.37%) > BH 50/50 (-0.54%). VT Robust becomes PT-preferred at λ=1.52 (mild loss aversion, well below standard 2.25). 12/VIX never becomes preferred (higher equity tilt = more loss exposure). Risk Parity breaks even at λ=1.06 (any loss aversion at all). PT ranking at λ=2.25: Risk_Parity > VT_Robust > BH_5050 > VT_12VIX > BH_SPY. AMPLIFICATION: mean return says VT Robust is -26bps/yr worse, but PT CE says +6bps/yr better — loss aversion converts tail protection into preference reversal. IMPLICATION: VT's value cannot be assessed by Sharpe alone. For real investors with loss aversion (everyone), VT Robust is objectively better insurance. This strengthens Paper 4 (insurance cost) narrative: the 'cost' of VT is an illusion under PT.

title: K861: Oil-Equity Vol Channel — Oil DROPS Drive Equity Vol (t=5.82), Not Spikes (t=0.70). Asymmetric.
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K861 tests oil price shocks as climate/macro proxy for equity vol prediction. Data: SPY/XLE/DBA/CL=F 2007-2026 (4,839 days). KEY FINDING: Strong asymmetry — oil DROPS increase SPY RV by +4.8pp (t=5.82 Harvey PASS), but oil SPIKES only +0.7pp (t=0.70 NS). Oil drops signal demand destruction/recession fears (Kilian 2009). Oil vol regime predicts forward SPY vol: high oil vol → 19.0% vs low → 13.6% (t=16.82). BUT reverse Granger is stronger (SPY→Oil F=11-49 vs Oil→SPY F<10) — shared macro risk, not clean causal channel. XLE most sensitive (β=0.52), DBA weakest (β=0.12). Post-2020 effect slightly larger but not Harvey significant. LIMITATION: oil is proxy, not direct climate data. CONCLUSION: Oil vol is a COINCIDENT indicator of equity stress (not leading), and the asymmetry (drops > spikes) is the publishable finding.

Spread captures microstructure liquidity risk that VIX doesn't. BUT: does NOT improve HAR models (HAR-S vs HAR DM all NS). OOS Spearman: Spread+VIX (0.377) slightly > VIX alone (0.374). TAIWAN: 0050.TW spread not significant (t=2.33, bivariate t=1.95). Different market microstructure. REGIME: larger beta in high-VIX (0.070 vs 0.008). CONCLUSION: OHLC spread is a useful VIX complement for US vol monitoring but doesn't materially improve forecasting models. Cross-market microstructure differences are real.

title: K863: Phase Transition Detection NULL — Physics Indicators AUC 0.514 < VIX 0.555, VIX Sufficiency #25

Data: SPY/QQQ/GLD/TLT/EEM/VIX 2005-2026 (5,346 days, 15 crashes). 3 indicators: cross-asset correlation order parameter (AUC 0.506), Shannon entropy (AUC 0.440 wrong direction), critical slowing down VIX AR1 (AUC 0.517). All worse than VIX level (AUC 0.631). OOS composite: 0.514 vs VIX-only 0.555 — physics indicators HURT by adding noise. Lead-lag shows indicators DO rise before crashes, but VIX rises faster. Trading test: no phase strategy beats 12/VIX (DM t=-4.55). Precision 23.5% at 90th pct threshold (76.5% false alarms). Confirms K98. VIX SUFFICIENCY #25. Cross-discipline approach explored but VIX remains the sufficient statistic.

title: K864: Heterogeneous ABM ★★ — Strategy Diversity AMPLIFIES Crowding (Flash Crashes +592%, Vol +53%), Opposite of Hypothesis
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] K864 tests whether strategy heterogeneity reduces VT crowding (K827 extension). 1000 agents, 200 noise fixed, 4 VT types (12/VIX, Floor+Cap, Risk Parity, EWMA), 2600 sims. SHOCKING RESULT: Heterogeneity makes crowding WORSE. At 50% adoption: flash crashes +592% (3.2/yr vs 0.46/yr), market vol +53% (0.29 vs 0.19), MDD -31% worse. Tipping point unchanged at 50%. MECHANISM: Diverse strategies create asynchronous multi-wave selling cascades — Type A sells first (aggressive), then Type D days later (EWMA lag), then Type C (risk parity reacts to realized vol). Persistent sequential selling is harder for market to absorb than one sharp simultaneous impact. PARADOX: Individual VT agents have BETTER Sharpe in heterogeneous regime (0.376 vs 0.083 at 70%) because diverse responses smooth individual portfolios even as they destroy the market. PAPER 5 IMPLICATION: This was Limitation #4 of K827v3. Relaxing homogeneity assumption makes crowding WORSE — 'diverse strategies cancel out' intuition is WRONG.
data_source: Monte Carlo simulation (2600 sims, 1000 agents, 2520 days)

title: K906: SPY HAR-RV Preliminary — GJR Wins on Unified Targets (Overnight 50% of Total Vol)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] PRELIMINARY (29 OOS days). SPY 5-min data (55 days, Jan-Apr 2026). title: K907: Volatility Spillover Network — TCI ≠ VIX (r=0.001), Genuinely New Risk Dimension ★★
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Diebold-Yilmaz (2012/2014) connectedness analysis on 9 assets (SPY/QQQ/IWM/EFA/EEM/0050.TW/GLD/TLT/USO), 4476 trading days (2009-2026). Garman-Klass vol proxy. VAR(5) + GFEVD (H=10). Rolling 250-day windows (4227 windows). KEY FINDING: Total Connectedness Index (TCI) = 50.0% — half of vol forecast error is cross-asset spillover. TCI-VIX Pearson r = 0.001 (p=0.93) — near zero! TCI captures fundamentally different info from VIX: network structure vs vol level. During COVID TCI-VIX r=0.74 but normally diverge. SPY is dominant net transmitter (NET=+34.8%), Taiwan 0050.TW is clear net receiver (NET=-18.4%, receives 27.9% from others mainly SPY, transmits 9.4%). USO most isolated (TO=1.9%). GLD relatively isolated (NET=-5.5%), supporting diversifier role. Robust across lag orders (50.0-50.7%), horizons (47.5-50.9%), windows (46.4-48.0%). This is NOT a VIX sufficiency confirmation — TCI is orthogonal to VIX, a genuinely new dimension. Potential: TCI as VT overlay (reduces when connected?), portfolio construction timing.

title: K908: MF-GJR + Student-t/HistSim — Complete VaR/ES Solution ★★★
content: [提出: 用戶, 執行: Claude] Fills K889 VaR gap. 5 model-distribution combos (GJR+Normal, GJR+Student-t, MF-GJR+Normal, MF-GJR+Student-t, MF-GJR+HistSim) on SPY/QQQ/0050.TW. Student-t df re-estimated each 63d refit with sqrt((df-2)/df) scale correction. RESULTS: MF-GJR+Student-t achieves 1% Trinity PASS for SPY (22/1821=1.21%, Kupiec p=0.387) and 0050.TW (17/1754=0.97%, p=0.896), but FAILS QQQ (30/1821=1.65%). MF-GJR+HistSim achieves 1% Trinity PASS for ALL 3 assets (6/6 pass) — universal solution. SPY Student-t df~6-9, QQQ 6-11, 0050.TW 4.7-6.6 (heaviest tails, Student-t most effective). ES Acerbi-Szekely: SPY p=0.059 marginal. Fissler-Ziegel confirms MF-GJR+HistSim ranks #1 overall. KEY INSIGHT: Best prediction model (MF-GJR, K889) + correct tail distribution (HistSim) = complete solution for both forecasting AND risk management. Two orthogonal dimensions independently optimized.

title: K909: MF-GJR Extended Factors — No Harvey PASS Beyond VIX (VIX Sufficiency #26)
content: [提出: 用戶, 執行: Claude] Tested 3 additional long-run factors in MF-GJR multiplicative framework: (1) VIX term structure slope (log(VIX3M/VIX)), (2) Corwin-Schultz OHLC spread, (3) Parkinson range. τ_t = exp(θ₀ + θ₁×logVIX + θ₂×X). CS Spread: SPY t=-2.11 NS, theta_2 hits bound (scaling issue). Range: t=-0.36 NS. VIX Slope negative coefficient = backwardation predicts higher vol beyond VIX level (economically intuitive). MCS for SPY: only VIX+Slope survives (eliminates VIX-only). But Harvey threshold not met. VIX sufficiency confirmed #26. MF-GJR(VIX) remains the recommended model — adding complexity does not reliably improve.

title: K910: TCI as VT Overlay — NULL (Structural Descriptor, Not Trading Signal)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Tested K907 TCI as VT strategy overlay. 4 strategies (TCI Defensive, TCI+VIX Combined, Smooth TCI, TCI Div Timing) vs 3 baselines (BH SPY, BH 50/50, 12/VIX). OOS 2009-2026 (~16yr). RESULT: 0/4 strategies pass Harvey DM test vs any baseline. TCI+VIX Combined Sharpe 0.992 vs 50/50 0.973 but DM t=-0.28 (NS). TCI vs next-day return r=0.005 (p=0.77, zero directional prediction). TCI vs 21d vol r=0.067 (p<0.001, weak vol prediction). CONCLUSION: TCI is a structural descriptor of cross-asset connectedness, NOT a trading signal. Consistent with K697 (VIX predicts vol magnitude not direction). TCI value is in understanding market structure (who transmits, who receives), not in timing strategies.

title: K911: Quantile Connectedness — Left-Tail ≈ Mean (r=0.952), Right-Tail Independent (r=0.017)
content: [提出: Gemini G3-2, 執行: Claude] Quantile VAR connectedness at τ=0.05/0.50/0.95 on 4 assets (SPY/QQQ/GLD/0050.TW), rolling 250d step=5. KEY: Left-tail TCI(τ=0.05) tracks Mean TCI(τ=0.50) almost perfectly (r=0.952) — hypothesis that tail is different from mean REJECTED for left tail. But Right-tail TCI(τ=0.95) IS independent (r=0.017 vs mean), averages ~70% (much higher), nearly constant across regimes. Tail TCI-VIX r=0.399 (moderate, 4-asset composition effect vs K907 9-asset r=0.001). Tail risk prediction weak: AUC=0.581 (marginal). COVID spike 2.0x for left/mean, but right-tail barely moved (1.07x). Negative logistic coefficient (counterintuitive: high TCI → fewer tail events, possibly because TCI rises AFTER onset). CONCLUSION: Looking at quantile tails does not rescue TCI as a trading signal. Left-tail ≈ mean. Right-tail is independent but constant (no variation to exploit). TCI remains a structural descriptor.

title: K912: MF-GJR Regime Decomposition ★★ — Advantage Strongest in LOW VIX (t=-3.98), Not Crisis
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Decomposed MF-GJR vs GJR advantage across VIX regimes for SPY (OOS 2019-2026, 1821 days). SURPRISING: MF-GJR advantage strongest in LOW VIX (<15): DM t=-3.98 Harvey PASS, win rate 70.1%. Medium (15-25): t=-2.46, 50.9%. High (25-35): t=-1.43 NS, 45.1%. Crisis (>35): t=-0.04 NS, 33.9%. Point estimate largest in High VIX (+0.212) but variance too large. Tau contribution: 66%(Low)→71%(Med)→51%(High)→82%(Crisis). Rolling advantage positive 83.9% of time. Advantage-VIX correlation r=0.359. COVID showed largest event advantage (+0.280). INTERPRETATION: MF-GJR adds value by precisely capturing the tau/VIX relationship during calm periods when short-run g_t is stable. During crises, both models struggle equally with extreme returns. This is COUNTER-INTUITIVE but makes sense: multiplicative structure matters most when the long-run component is the dominant driver (low vol, stable g). Paper angle: MF-GJR is a precision model for normal times, not a crisis tool.

title: K913: VRP Return Prediction — NULL at All Horizons (OOS R² Negative)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Variance Risk Premium (VRP = VIX² - RV_22d) as SPY return predictor. 2006-2026, IS/OOS split 2019. VRP positive 85.7% (fear premium persistent), mean=0.0081, VRP-VIX r=-0.24 (distinct). RESULT NULL: No horizon significant — daily t=1.10, weekly t=0.37, monthly t=0.23 (all fail Harvey). MDD improvement -37.4% vs -59.6% (risk reduction, not alpha). VRP does NOT improve 12/VIX (combined 0.39 vs plain 0.59). CONCLUSION: VRP exists as structural options market premium but cannot be reliably timed. Consistent with K697 (direction unpredictable). VRP benefit = risk reduction = drawdown insurance (same as VT). Bollerslev et al. (2009) in-sample result does not survive our strict OOS + Harvey criteria.

title: K914: Overnight-Intraday Decomposed MF-GJR — NULL (VIX Already Captures Structure)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Decomposed SPY returns into overnight (close→open) and intraday (open→close). Overnight variance share 36.2%, intraday 60.1%, cov 3.7%. Nearly uncorrelated (r=0.039). VIX correlates more with intraday r² (0.354) than overnight (0.293). Strong bidirectional Granger causality. 4 models tested: A=standard MF-GJR, B=+overnight r² regressor, C=separate overnight+intraday MF-GJR, D=+overnight ratio. OOS 2019-2026 (1821d). RESULT NULL: No model passes Harvey. B: t=-0.73 NS (theta2 hits bound). C: -0.36% QLIKE but t=-0.92 NS. D: WORSE (+0.28%, t=+2.78 wrong direction). CONCLUSION: VIX elasticity in MF-GJR tau already implicitly captures overnight/intraday structure. Adding explicit decomposition is redundant. VIX is forward-looking and integrates all vol sources. MF-GJR(VIX) remains optimal — cannot be improved by decomposing what VIX already knows.

title: K915: DCC-GARCH Dynamic Correlation — Real Dynamics but Portfolio NULL (50/50 Irreducible #11)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] DCC-GARCH(1,1) on SPY/GLD/TLT (2005-2026). DCC params: a=0.032, b=0.955, persistence=0.988. Static 1/3 each best Sharpe (0.811) and lowest MDD (-24.0%). CONCLUSION: DCC captures real dynamics but cannot be profitably exploited due to turnover. 50/50 irreducible #11. But DCC as analytical tool is valuable — reveals 2022 as structural break in stock-bond correlation.

title: K916: MF-GJR on Bitcoin — VIX Elasticity 31% of SPY, Harvey FAIL but Meaningful Null
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] MF-GJR on BTC-USD (2015-2026, OOS 2021-2026). BTC vol 61.1% (3.44x SPY). VIX-BTC correlation only 0.055 (SPY: 0.547, 10x stronger). title: K918: BEKK-GARCH SPY-GLD — No Cross-Spillover (LR p=0.112), Independence IS Diversification
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Full BEKK(1,1) vs Diagonal BEKK on SPY+GLD (2005-2026). LR test stat=7.50, p=0.112 — Diagonal preferred (no cross-spillover needed). title: K919: DASN SPY→Taiwan — Gap Channel Dominates 99.7% (R²=0.355), Intraday Near Zero ★★
content: [提出: Gemini G3-1, 執行: Claude] Decomposed SPY→0050.TW transmission into overnight gap and intraday channels. 2012-2026. Lead-lag corr: SPY(T)→TW overnight(T+1)=0.596 vs SPY(T)→TW intraday(T+1)=-0.039. 0050.TW variance: overnight 53.1%, intraday 42.5%. VIX regime: high VIX gap R²=0.408 vs low VIX=0.223 (monotonic). Night session (2017/05): gap R² increased 0.331→0.363 (contrary to expectation — night session increased connectivity). Intraday beta turns negative in high VIX (mean reversion). Granger: SPY→TW confirmed all lags. PRACTICAL: Taiwan investors should focus on pre-market US close. By open, information is priced in. Intraday chasing is unproductive.

title: K920: Copula-GARCH SPY/GLD ★★ — Student-t Best, λ=0.14 Symmetric, But Gold Decouples in Crises
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Copula-GARCH on SPY/GLD (2005-2026). 5 copulas tested: Gaussian/Student-t/Clayton/Gumbel/Frank. Student-t dominates by AIC (delta>195 vs Clayton). KEY: Symmetric tail dependence λ_L=λ_U≈0.14 (copula df≈3.0, much lower than marginal GARCH dfs 5-6). SPY-GLD have meaningful non-linear co-movement in extremes. BUT crisis behavior is diversification-friendly: GFC Clayton λ_L=0.007, COVID Student-t ρ=-0.147 and λ dropped to 0.068. Gold decouples precisely when needed most. 2022 rate hike anomalous: positive corr (0.194) but lowest λ (0.049). VaR 5% passes all tests; 1% too liberal (1.7% violations, Basel Red). CONCLUSION: 50/50 moat is NUANCED — statistical λ=0.14 means imperfect diversification in tails, but behavioral/structural decoupling in crises means the moat is real. The moat is not statistical independence but crisis-conditional independence.

title: K921: Time-Varying Copula — Dynamic λ Real but Early Warning 1/3 Only (VIX Drives λ, Not Reverse)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Patton (2006) time-varying Student-t copula on SPY/GLD. AIC delta=-143.6 vs static (strongly preferred, LR p<0.0001). Dynamic ρ_t range [-0.59,+0.59], mean=0.078. λ_t range [0.016,0.366], mean=0.147. 9 regime breaks detected. EARLY WARNING: 1/3 crises only — COVID 2020 YES (λ declining, trend=-0.000635/d, R²=0.27), GFC 2008 NO (λ increasing), Rate Hike 2022 NO (λ increasing). Granger: VIX→λ F=9.38 p=0.002 (strong), λ→VIX F=2.62 p=0.033 (marginal). VIX drives tail dependence, not reverse. λ(t) vs VIX(t+22) r=0.013 (negligible). VaR both too conservative (1.1-1.7% actual vs 5% expected). CONCLUSION: Dynamic copula is real improvement over static, but λ_t is not a reliable early warning — VIX causes λ changes, so λ contains no independent lead information.

title: K922: Copula SPY-0050.TW ★★ — Higher Corr but Lower Tail Dep (λ=0.078), COVID Amplified (0.364)
content: [提出: Claude, 執行: Claude] Copula-GARCH on SPY/0050.TW (2006-2026). Student-t copula best (same as K920 SPY-GLD). KEY: SPY-0050.TW ρ=0.219 (2.3x SPY-GLD 0.094) but λ=0.078 (HALF of SPY-GLD 0.140). Higher ν=5.75 (vs 3.05) = thinner joint tails despite stronger average correlation. BUT GFC λ=0.000 and Rate Hike λ=0.000 — 0050.TW actually decoupled in US-originated crises (contradicts hypothesis). COPULA MOAT EXPLANATION: GLD decouples from SPY in crises (K920), 0050.TW amplifies during global events but decouples during US-specific events. SPY/GLD preferred over SPY/0050.TW because GLD provides CONSISTENT crisis protection while 0050.TW is unpredictable. Portfolio VaR: SPY/TW historical tail -2.68% vs SPY/GLD -2.39% (worse). Directly supports Paper 2 Taiwan VT.
